correctness.rationale: For the solid cap R>0, 0<t<=2, u=2−t, axial density proportional to 1−z² and conditional transverse uniform disks yield Z_j=∫z^j(1−z²)dz/∫(1−z²)dz. Independent expansion of ||X−Y||² and ||X−Y||⁴ gives M1=R²*3(2−u)A/[40(1+u)²], M2=R⁴*(2−u)²B/[70(1+u)²], A=7u³+14u²+20u+8, B=41u⁴+82u³+99u²+108u+36. Q=160(1+u)²B/(63A²); exact differentiation gives Q'=3200(1+u)u²(66u³+117u²+56u+12)/(63A³)>0 for 0<u<2, with Q(0)=10/7, Q(2−)=7/4 and Q−10/7=(25/63)u³+O(u⁴). Thus Q determines shape, M1 fixes R, inverse has sharp 1/3 Hölder at the full ball. Independently recomputed polynomial integrals/derivative/cubic coefficient symbolically, not relying on Monte Carlo. No noisy statistical assertion.

value.rationale: Solid spherical caps form a canonical two-parameter convex-body model, and two independent-point Euclidean even distance moments are natural stereological observations. The exact feasible ratio interval, unique global inverse and optimal cubic ill-conditioning at the full ball are precise, nonmechanical, potentially useful shape-identification results; not simply a known inertia table.
